newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange gets Australian nod.
newsitem.headline: Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange gets Australian nod.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) said on Wednesday it had been granted the status of "approved foreign stock exchange" by the Australian Securities Commission.
"The approved foreign stock exchange status, which relates to both the Main and Second Boards of the KLSE, came into effect on July 2, 1997," said the exchange in a statement.
"One of the main benefits would be that Australian broking houses can promote Malaysian stocks more effectively and with fewer restrictions to Australian investors," the KLSE said.
KLSE-listed companies would also now be able to more easily offer securities to Australian shareholders, possibly making Malaysian shares more attractive to Australian investors, it said.
The approval would also raise the likelihood of the secondary listing of Malaysian listed companies on the Australian Stock Exchange, the KLSE said.
